_meta.purpose: Ambient residents: the persistent third tier between the 14 named NPCs and the CrowdSystem transients. Created once on location enter, torn down on exit, never routed away, barks only.
_meta.coordinateSpace: NATIVE plate px, keyed by location id. station/route are sprite ORIGIN points; feet are at y+15. LocationData merges these into the location runtime and scales exactly once.
_meta.whyNotInLocationFiles: src/data/locations/*.location.json is REGENERATED by the plate compositor, which would silently drop hand-authored additions. Residents are authored, not composited, so they live here and are merged at load.
_meta.sprites: Crowd sheets already registered in BootScene. No new art.

rua-direita.role: Water carrier at the public well
barks: Two trips before the sun is over the arcade, or the queue is longer than the rope.
Mind the spill, tuan. Wet stone and Portuguese boots are old enemies.
The well never runs dry here. The street above it does, but never the well.
My grandmother drew from this well when there was a sultan to draw it for.
You want cool water? Come at six. After noon it tastes of the whole street.
Everyone is careful with their doors this week. Even the ones with nothing behind them.
The spice merchant came for water himself this morning. Smiling. I nearly dropped the bucket.
Hoop, head, stave. Get one wrong and the sea finds it for you.
Every cask on this street was mine or was made badly.
Green wood in this heat? It will open like a flower halfway to Goa.
Stand back a pace, friend, unless you want a mallet through the sandal.
Alvares wants forty by Friday. Alvares always wants forty by Friday.

rua-direita.role: Porter waiting for a load under the arcade
barks: You need something carried, you say so. I am standing here either way.
Two coins to the gate, three to the quay. The hill is five and I will not argue.
A man who runs in this heat arrives sweating and gets paid the same.
The lighters came up short today. Short lighters, short work.
I have carried tin, silk, pepper and a Jesuit's library. The library was worst.
Forty bolts sitting bonded at the gate and not one of them needing a back. Bad week.
Kembung, selar, prawns as long as your hand! Same three prices, same as yesterday.
You will not get it cheaper on the hill and it will not be this fresh.
Buy it now or buy it grilled in an hour, but you will buy it.
The nakhoda takes two every evening and pays without looking. That is a customer.
Do not squeeze it. Everyone squeezes it. It does not tell you anything.
Something went out of a window on this quay. I sell fish. I saw fish.
Out to the junk and back, forty times today. I counted to forty twice.
You want the ships? I row. Cheap. Cheaper than falling in.
The Fujian one has eyes painted on her. She can see where she is going. I can too.
Nobody tips a boy. Everyone tips a boatman. I am waiting to become a boatman.
Do not step on the thwart. Step on the thwart and we both swim.

waterfront.role: Tallyman checking bales at the godowns
barks: Bale, mark, book. If the three do not agree, the book is right and I am wrong.
Bonded means it does not move. It moves anyway, and then I write why.
Five hundred bahar of pepper in that shed and a seal on the door that keeps getting mended.
Do not lean on the stack. Roped is not the same as safe.
The counting house wants the tally by dusk. The counting house always wants it by dusk.
Move along the wall side. The middle is for carts.
Papers at the table, not at me. I only look at faces.
Eighty of us and two hundred auxiliaries, they say. I have never once counted eighty.
The Capitão walks the rack at nine. Be somewhere else at nine.
Four hours to go. Then four hours of sleep, then four hours of this.
nightBarks: Gate is shut. Whatever it is, it keeps until six.
You are out late for a man with nowhere to be.
Quiet night. I prefer the loud ones — you know where everybody is.

barks: *does not step aside* You are the one they brought up from the quay.
New inspector weighs everything twice. Queue is out to the padrão. Nobody pays anybody now.
Everything the queue forgot to bring. Water, rope, string, a comb.
Sit in the queue long enough and you will want what I am selling.
The gate opens at six and I open at half five. That is the whole business.
No, I do not sell papers. Everyone asks. Nobody laughs.
The soldiers pay. Slowly, and short, but they pay.

a-famosa-gate.role: Woman drawing at the praça well
barks: The praça well is sweeter than the street well. Do not tell the street.
They built this wall with stone from the Sultan's mosque. My mother would not drink here.
I drink here. My mother was a harder woman than I am.
The soldiers water their horses at the trough and their oaths at the tavern.
Careful of the pelourinho. Not the stone. The people who watch it.
Two feet of soil, then coral rock. Everyone here is buried shallower than they think.
Fever mostly. Fever, and the ones who go home in a barrel of arrack instead.
The Padre reads over every one of them. Even the ones nobody claims.
This ground was a chief's house before it was a church. Older bones underneath.
Do not stand on the ledger slabs, senhor. Somebody paid a great deal for that stone.
Three months. They tell me it becomes a habit. It has become a habit.
He sailed for Banda and came back as a name on a manifest.
The sailors' cross is for the ones with no ground. There are more of those.
You can see the strait from here. I do not know if that is kindness or not.
The Padre is good to me. He does not tell me it was God's plan. He knows better than that.
Mass at six, again at noon, vespers at six. The bell is not a suggestion.
Father Tomás will see anyone. Anyone at all. It is not always convenient.
Xavier himself preached on this hill. I am told so twice a week.
The brazier is for the damp, not the cold. Nothing here is ever cold.
Mind the step. Every soul in Melaka has caught a toe on that step.
The confessional is open until vespers. It is open to everyone. I only mention it.
Songket takes a month. People from the town want it by Thursday.
The gold thread comes up from the harbour. Everything comes up from the harbour.
Sit under the rain tree if you are waiting. Everyone waits under the rain tree.
My mother wove for the palace. There is no palace. I weave for whoever comes.
Do not buy cloth in the sun. Buy it in the shade and it will still be that colour tomorrow.
Mak Enang says I am not to run near the pots. I am not near the pots.
Are you from the fort? You do not look like the fort.
There is a boat at the landing with a hole in it. Pak Salleh says it is fine.
The rain tree is home. If you touch the rain tree you cannot be caught.
My sister is learning letters at the market. I am learning to run faster than her.

kampung.role: Elder on the mats by the surau
barks: Sit. You have been walking since the gate and it shows in your feet.
Zuhr is called from that door. You will hear it whether you want to or not.
The Portuguese count the fort and the church. Nobody counts us. It has advantages.
This mortar is older than the fortress. It has done more useful work.
Stay for the rice. Do not stay for the opinions.
A Portuguese and a Chinese signing together. The river has seen stranger things, but not this month.
